title: Tides
text: Ocean tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined gravitational pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun, together with the rotation of the Earth.

title: Spring and neap tides
text: When the Sun and Moon align at new and full moon their pulls add up and the range of the tide is largest; these are called spring tides, while neap tides occur at the quarter moons.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis: chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs sunlight, and the captured energy splits water and drives the conversion of carbon dioxide into glucose, releasing oxygen.

title: Chlorophyll
text: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green; it sits in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast.

title: Olympus Mons
text: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the Solar System, a shield volcano about 22 kilometres high and roughly the size of the state of Arizona.

title: Earth's largest volcano
text: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the largest active volcano on Earth by volume, rising more than four kilometres above sea level, but it is far smaller than Olympus Mons.

title: The Moon
text: The Moon orbits the Earth at an average distance of about 384 400 kilometres and its gravity is the main driver of the tides.

title: Solar energy
text: Solar panels turn sunlight directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect, a different process from the one plants use to store energy in sugar.
